room.scenario: Can we proceed with the decision in this Query, and under what conditions?

steps.text: Scenario: go-live slips one quarter. A one-quarter slip costs about AED 2.1m (parallel running AED 0.9m, contractor cover AED 0.8m, extra rehearsal and retraining AED 0.4m) against an undrawn AED 2.4m contingency, leaving AED 0.3m. The delay is affordable on these figures. But it is not free, and AED 2.1m of parallel running trains nobody: a slip only pays if it fixes the constraint. Two caveats I would put to the board: the estimate excludes CoreSys fees after 31 March 2027, which could eat the AED 0.3m and more; the 2027 forecast's downside liquidity is already narrower; and nobody has costed the other branch, a failed Q1 cutover and rollback, so the board is pricing only the cost of waiting. Position: the delay is affordable; hold Q1 to a hard gate on 16 December and slip only if the gate fails. Scripted position.

result.reasoningSummary: Recommendation for the 16 December board (D-114): do not approve a Q1 go-live on today's evidence; approve it conditionally. Q1 proceeds only if, by the board: (1) rehearsal 3 reconciles inside the 0.5% tolerance; (2) the trainer contract is signed and regional dates are confirmed; (3) owners are named for the intercompany and fixed-asset workstreams, so R-22 can be re-rated below high; (4) Legal has read clause 14.2 of the CoreSys agreement. If any condition fails, slip one quarter: about AED 2.1m, inside the AED 2.4m contingency, before CoreSys fees. Before the board, Finance should also cost a failed Q1 cutover and rollback: today only the cost of waiting is priced. Three variables drive the call: reconciliation, training and vendor support. The flip assumption is that CoreSys support can run past 31 March 2027 at a price inside the remaining AED 0.3m. If it cannot, neither date is safe and the board faces a vendor decision, not a timing one; and if the cited 90-day notice is right, that decision is due about two weeks after the board. Proposed owners: the Programme Director for the checklist and the R-22 re-rating, Procurement with Legal for CoreSys, People Operations for training, the Financial Controller for reconciliation sign-off. Owners, conditions and agent positions are scripted judgements, not recorded decisions.
